text:
Angel Mother Jennifer Bos urges Senate to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general
N. E. Ball
Illinois Angel Mother Jennifer Bos and a coalition of over 300 Angel Families called on the Senate to confirm Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche during the second day of hearings before the Senate Judiciary Committee, according to a July 21 statement.
Bos testified before the committee, saying, “I couldn't save my daughter, but Todd Blanche, as Attorney General, he might save yours… From the time that I've spent talking with Todd Blanche, I knew immediately that he makes victims a priority. Under his direction, the DOJ has engaged directly with the Angel Families and treated us not like political props, but as partners in preventing future tragedies.”
In an interview with Fox News Digital following her Capitol Hill testimony, Bos described her meeting with Blanche. “I immediately felt so pulled towards him,” she said. “You get a certain energy from people, and he is just the kindest. ... He listened to my story very intently, and you could just see his mind ticking like, 'what are we going to do about this?'”
Bos’s daughter Megan was found dead in April after disappearing for 51 days; Luis Mendoza-Gonzalez was charged in connection with her death. Due to Illinois' sanctuary policies, Mendoza-Gonzalez was initially released after a hearing but later arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Indiana after Bos shared her story at an anti-fentanyl bill signing event.
Bos told Fox News Digital that while nothing can be done for her own family now that her daughter has died, she believes Blanche understands what Angel Families face: "We're trying to make a difference for people who haven't been touched by this kind of tragedy." She also said she trusts Blanche is "doing the right thing for the right reasons" since being appointed acting attorney general following Pam Bondi's ouster.
During her testimony before the committee—which is responsible for legislative oversight affecting constitutional protections and public safety nationwide, according to its official website—Bos urged senators not to delay confirmation: "I'm asking the committee not to wait until another mother is sitting where I am. Confirm Todd Blanche," she said. "He is a leader who will uphold the law, honor victims, confront dangerous criminal organizations and fight to give other American families the safety and lasting protection that came too late for mine."
